# Spiritual Translation: The Five Degrees of Divine Operation Against Evil

---

**¶1:** [GAP-1] Evil and falsity — it was overcome by five degrees of divine operation proceeding from the Divine Itself.

**¶2:** The first degree is the Divine Itself, existing in infinite peace and hiddenness, established in its own celestial good, in its own infinite being.

**¶3:** Four further degrees of divine operation were made manifest and proceeded from the Divine Itself. They were appointed according to a fullness of truths in every degree, and established in a complete totality of all goods and truths together.

**¶4:** The second degree of divine operation poured forth and was made manifest. It was revealed from the Divine Itself. It is the proceeding of divine spiritual life, the Divine Spirit, together with the celestial human and his five faculties of celestial good — these constitute the second degree.

**¶5:** The third degree is the divine love of all wisdom, the power of divine ordering, the divine truth in its judicial and governing power, and the five derivative capacities of that governing truth. These constitute the third degree.

**¶6:** The fourth degree is divine providence proceeding into all things, and the sustaining power of divine truth that unites the lowest to the highest, and all the capacities of wisdom revealed through it. These constitute the fourth degree.

**¶7:** The fifth degree proceeding from the Divine Itself is divine illuminating wisdom, and all its powers which it summoned — its emanations which were [GAP-2] made to proceed. They poured forth and were manifested from it.

**¶8:** This is the manner in which they were distributed and [GAP-3] arranged in fives: these five [GAP-4: REVIEW — faculties] of the celestial human [GAP-5] constitute the whole spiritual edifice; another five are the five capacities of divine truth in its governing power, which are distributed to five distinct planes of existence, sustaining [GAP-6] all things therein.

**¶9:** [GAP-7] In complete totality across all planes, which [GAP-8: ... There are] two further principles joined to them — the calling forth of divine truth and its reciprocal reception. These are the active influx and the receptive will — the father-principle and the mother-principle — whom divine illuminating wisdom, by its advent, appointed as continuing presences in its own function [GAP-9] within the great celestial good and the [GAP-10] abiding in them.

**¶10:** [GAP-11: The descent] of the celestial human who came [GAP-12] belonging to [GAP-13] existing in a state of spiritual dominion [GAP-14] held in honor before those of his own household [GAP-15], yet his adversaries [GAP-16] afflicted him and oppressed him through their wickedness; and they stripped from him [GAP-17] his spiritual abundance; and they imprisoned [GAP-18: REVIEW — him in] bondage and seized from him his companion affections. Yet he [GAP-19] prevailed by his humility; and he took courage and restrained his adversary [GAP-20] in patient stillness.

**¶11:** Just as with such a one — this noble interior good whose adversaries surround him — so also is the manner of the descent of the celestial human, [GAP-21] among the ruling evils, the adversaries of wisdom.

**¶12:** In contrast, the advent of divine truth in its judicial power, and the commission it received, whereby it came upon all the ruling evils — this differs from the descent of the celestial human. Its advent [GAP-22] differs from the descent of the celestial human.

**¶13:** The advent of divine truth in its judicial power is of this nature: when it was sent from the Divine Itself so that it might raise up the celestial human. It resembles a righteous judge whom the sovereign good would send to overturn the violence done to that one — the noble interior good against whom his adversaries had transgressed. And this judge [GAP-23] was severe and unyielding [GAP-24] and provided the means [GAP-25] through his righteousness and his power; and he also judged all who were condemned according to their rebellious will, and rendered to each according to his deserts. Those deserving of chastisement he struck with harsh correction. Those deserving of the severing of their faculties, or indeed their [GAP-26] — he rendered to them accordingly. [GAP-27] And he bound them and constrained them and suspended them by [GAP-28] — and thus he did to them with righteous judgment. And he destroyed them to strip away their external appearances [GAP-29] so that they should be annihilated by a spiritual death [GAP-30] utterly. Again, [GAP-31: REVIEW — those for] whom it is fitting [GAP-32] to be expelled from their states, he removed by righteous judgment; just as they had transgressed and sinned against the noble interior good.

**¶14:** Also, the companion powers in the hidden operation and the attendants of this divine truth in judgment — those who belong to it in great strength — in an instant and with urgency they accomplish the will of their lord.

**¶15:** Now, just as this righteous judge was sent from the sovereign good to overturn the violence done to the noble interior good: so also is it with divine truth in its judicial power. It too was sent from the Lord of all wisdom to overturn the oppression and violence done to the celestial human, against whom the sovereign of the realms of falsity and evil had sinned. He transgressed and sinned against him, together with all his rebellious powers. Therefore, when divine truth in judgment came, it bore up the celestial human.

**¶16:** Also, all the ruling evils — the powers of transgression who had sinned against the faculties of the celestial human — it has judged them according to righteous judgment. It has bound them in both internal and external states. It placed each one in the condition befitting it; it weighed each of them according to its cruelty and oppression. Some of them it enclosed within restraint; others it inverted — reversing their very order. Some [GAP-33] were fixed immovably in their own evil; others were set in permanent confinement. Some among them were placed beneath their companions, restricted by bonds that cannot be broken; others were made to have dominion over their companions below, so that the hells are ordered by their own hierarchies among those beneath them.

**¶17:** When the source of divine life established these judgments [GAP-34], it was revealed to all the powers of falsity and evil. It judged them as a true arbiter of what is just [GAP-35]. This is the first judgment that divine truth in its governing power rendered upon the ruling evils [GAP-36: REVIEW — in respect of] the celestial human. Indeed, it gave victory to the celestial human corresponding to his faithfulness; but it condemned the sovereign of the realms of falsity corresponding to the measure of his transgression.

**¶18:** [GAP-37] This restraint, of this kind, became [GAP-38] fixed in the natural order until the final consummation, when all the composite states shall be dissolved; and what is false perishes in the great fire of divine love and is separated. While wisdom returns to its own realm, falsity and evil remain in their bonds and restraint to eternity.

**¶19:** The advent also of divine providence, when it came to inspect those who are imprisoned in the intermediate sphere between good and evil: it is like a great sovereign who comes and inspects those who perform uses [GAP-39] and [GAP-40] and [GAP-41].

**¶20:** Also, those who are good among the spirits and angels who perform uses and who order truths and who labor in each plane — the sovereign sees that they have worked well and devoted themselves to their appointed tasks faithfully. He rejoices with great joy [GAP-42]. He acknowledges those who have built according to his purposes [GAP-43: REVIEW — and completed] his commands.

**¶21:** Now, just as this great sovereign who comes and inspects his ordered works and doctrinal defenses, so also is the advent of divine providence. For when it too came, it saw [GAP-44: REVIEW — its works] established and prepared and [GAP-45] the ordered series of ruling evils restrained and established, above and below, outwardly and inwardly, in the grand pattern that its fellow divine powers had fashioned. They had preceded it into the contest — they who had ordered and formed the entire spiritual cosmos before it arrived. It saw the celestial beings and angelic powers established and governing the defenses of truth [GAP-46], guarding the entire order of governance [GAP-47] — all of which the prior degrees of divine operation had accomplished. These are the celestial human, and divine truth in its judicial power, and the Divine Spirit proceeding as spiritual life.

**¶22:** Therefore, when divine providence beheld them — that they had created everything with great wisdom — [GAP-48] as they were made manifest it drew forth [GAP-49]. In its advent, by which it came, it was unveiled to them. It says to divine truth in its judicial power: "The judgment that you have [GAP-50] rendered is good; what you pronounced [GAP-51] you gave to them correspondingly, so that they were moved and elevated beyond what they had merited."

**¶23:** The advent also of divine illuminating wisdom: the time when it came to all [GAP-52] — being just as if a man were sent to uproot a [GAP-53] and to burn a stubborn planting of false perceptions with fire. Therefore, when he has first cut down the evil perceptions with the sharp instrument of truth and has uprooted [GAP-54] their very substance with his fire, so that they cannot return to propagate from that time onward, nor produce works that are harmful to the spiritual life [GAP-55].

**¶24:** Afterward, he also planted genuine perceptions — the perception of life that yields good works.

**¶25:** Again, this is the spiritual meaning of the advent of divine illuminating wisdom. It happened in this manner: because it too set out [GAP-56] with its power and its wisdom, in its [GAP-57]-ness [GAP-58] as sovereign and redeemer [GAP-59], and in its glorious wisdom it destroyed the false perceptions. It bound them and broke them apart, as fire burns and destroys perverse growths of thought. This is also how it accomplished its will in the intermediate sphere, among the many powers of evil, until it reached the form of the natural humanity — the most ancient will and understanding, the first human faculties. [GAP-60: REVIEW — It perfected] its will in the receptive faculty; it [GAP-61]. It also gave hope to the volitional faculty, and the glad tidings [GAP-62] of glorious [GAP-63] purpose. It ascended to elevated states [GAP-64] of wisdom.

**¶26:** Then the calling forth of divine truth and its reciprocal reception — the great counsel that came to the basic elements of the natural mind, which are set in conjunction — it mixed with them, it was established in silence. It bears up [GAP-65] until the final consummation, when it can arise and stand firm in the great fire of divine love. It will gather to itself its own life, and form it in the Last Completed Human. You will also find it purges and casts from itself all defilement that is foreign to it. However, the life and the wisdom that are in all things, it gathers into itself and builds upon its spiritual body.

**¶27:** The time when this ultimate divine human form is perfected in all its faculties — then it becomes free and ascends from that great struggle through divine truth in its governing power, its father, the one who comes and brings a [GAP-66] faculty. He raises it up from within this gathering — the dissolution and consummation of all impermanent states.

**¶28:** Now, this counsel — that calling and reception — resembles thus: clarified good extracted from natural good. If a person takes it and places it into fervent natural good, it dissolves and pervades this fervent natural good. It works at another time in silence and stillness into the very center [GAP-67] — yet also, of the power and the essential quality of this natural good [GAP-68] it draws to itself, and the natural good settles and becomes still [GAP-69] in [GAP-70] and the [GAP-71]. The impurities of this natural good it clarifies and discards. However, the celestial good, the essential nourishment, and the beauty of the natural good — these it gathers into itself.

**¶29:** Again, this too is what the advent of that interior thought is — the counsel of life, which is the calling forth of divine truth and its reception, which came to the elements of the natural mind. This is the one that at the end can arise and stand firm, and will gather into itself all the lives and the wisdom that has remained within everything. It builds them upon its spiritual body; it gathers them into itself [GAP-72] into its own image forever and ever [GAP-73] from this time.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [...] the Darkness, it was defeated by five greatnesses.
The first greatness is the Father of Greatness who exists in calm and hiddenness; as he is established in his light-earth, in his own essence.
Four greatnesses were manifested and came forth of him. They were appointed to ten parts, and established in total twelve.

The second greatness poured out and was manifested. It was revealed from the first greatness. It is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, together with the First Man and his five sons; these are the second greatness.
The third greatness is the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder, the Living Spirit, and the five sons of the Living Spirit. These are the third greatness.
The fourth greatness is the Third Ambassador, and the Pillar of Glory, and all the light powers who were revealed from him. These are the fourth greatness.
The fifth greatness who came from the Father is Jesus the Splendour, and all his powers whom he summoned, his emanations who were [revealed from him] They poured out and were manifested from him.

This is, so that they were spread out and [established in] fives: these five [sons] of the First Man [who support] the entire building; another five are the five sons of the Living Spirit who are spread out to five places, supporting [all things]

[...] total in twelve parts that [... There are] another two added to them who are the summons and the obedience. They are the father and the mother whom Jesus the Splendour by his advent has appointed as successors to his place [over] the great earth and the [light] in them.

[The advent also] of the First Man who came [is like a man] belonging to [his father] existing in a kingdom [of great] esteem before they who belong to his household [...] his enemies [surrounded him] and suffering by their wickedness; and they take from him [his glory] and a richness; and they imprison [him in] captivity and take from him their companies (?). Yet, he [prevailed] by his humility; and he takes heart and restrains his enemy [...] in silence.
Just as with this man, this noble son whose enemies surround him, this also is how the advent of the First Man happened, [among the] rulers, the enemies of the light.

In contrast, the advent of the Living Spirit and the commandment that he received, whereby he came upon all the rulers, it differs from that of the First Man. His advent [is not like] the advent of the First Man.

The advent of the Living Spirit is like this, when he was sent from the greatness that he might bring up the First Man. He resembles a judge the king would send to overturn the violence to that man, the noble son against whom his enemies sinned. And he, this judge, [he is] hard and cruel [...] and he gives the means [to that man] by his righteousness and his strength; and he also judges all who are condemned according to their rebellious heart, and repays each according to his deserts. They who are worthy of blows he strikes with hard leather whips. Again, these who are worthy of cutting off their limbs, or indeed their [heads] and he repays them accordingly. [...] and he binds and fetters them, and hangs by [their feet] and thus he does to them with a righteous judgement. And he kills them to flay their skin [from them] so that they will be killed by a death [...] until they die. Again, [they for] whom it is fitting [...] to banish from their dwellings he may remove according to a righteous judgement; just as they had faulted and sinned against the noble son.
Also, the associates in the mystery and the assistants of this judge, these who belong to him in great strength; in an instant and haste they shall do the will of their master.

Now, just as this genuine judge, who was sent from the king to overturn the violence to this man, the noble son: this is also the case with the Living Spirit. He also was sent from the King of the lights to overturn the vengeance and violence to the First Man, against whom the King of the realms of Darkness had sinned. He faulted and sinned against him, and also his rebellious powers. Therefore, when (the Living Spirit) came, he bore up the First Man.

Also, all the rulers, the powers of sin who had faulted and sinned against the sons of the First Man, he has judged them according to a righteous judgement. He has bound them in heaven and earth. He put each one to the place fitting for him; he weighed each of them according to his cruelty and oppression. While some of them he enclosed in the prison, others he hung head down. Some [of them] are crucified, others are sat down all the time. Some among them are fixed beneath their associates, restricted by a strong chain; others he made the holders of authority over their companions beneath, so that they may do their pleasure amongst these below them.

when the Father of Life established the judgements [upon them] He was revealed to all the powers of Darkness. He judged them as a true giver of judgement [...] This is the first judgement that the Living Spirit gave the rulers [in respect of the] First Man. Indeed, he gave victory to the First Man corresponding to his victory; but he condemned the King of the realms of Darkness corresponding to that by which he had erred.

[...] this chain, of this sort, became [fixed in] the earth till the end time when the universe will be dissolved; and it perishes in the great fire and is separated. While the light goes to its country, the Darkness remains in the chain and fetter for ever.
The advent also of the Third Ambassador, when he came to inspect they who are imprisoned in the zone: he is like a great king who comes and inspects craftsmen [...] and [architects] and [artisans]

Also, they who are good, of the craftsmen and architects and artisans whom he has there in each place: he shall see that they have worked well, and have fallen to his works in their fashion. He shall rejoice with great joy [over them] He shall thank the artisans who have constructed his works [and completed] his orders.

Now, just as this great king who comes and inspects his works and fortifications, so also is the advent of the Third Ambassador. For, when he too came, he saw [his works] established and prepared and [also the] series of the rulers prepared and established there, above and below, outside and within, in the great pattern that his brothers had made. They had come before him to the contest, they who had fixed and created the universe before he came. He saw the gods and the angels established and controlling the fortifications [...] guarding the entire ruling-power [...] which his first powers had done. They are the First Man and the Living Spirit and the Great Spirit, the Mother of Life.

Therefore, when he saw them, that they had created everything with great wisdom, [...] as they looked he plundered (?) [...] in his advent, by which he came, he was unveiled to them. He says to the Living Spirit: "The judgement that you have [given is] good, what you uttered [is just] you gave to them correspondingly; so that they were moved and raised up to that of which they were not worthy".

The advent also of Jesus the Splendour, the time when he came to all [things] being just like a man if he is sent to pull out a [bad tree and] burn a difficult fig-garden with fire. Therefore, again, when he has first cut the bad trees with his axe and has pulled out [their roots] and their body with his fire, so that they should not return to sprout from this time, nor bear fruit bad to eat [any more]
Afterwards, he also planted good plants: the tree of life that will make good fruit.

Again, this is like this simile of the advent of Jesus the Splendour. It happened like this; because he too set out [...] his power and his wisdom, in his [righteous]-ness [...] a king and a saviour [...] in his glorious wisdom he destroyed them. He bound and crushed them like the fire that shall burn and destroy trees. This is also how he performed his will in the zone, among the many powers, until he reached the form of the flesh of Adam and Eve, the first humans. [He perfected] his will in Eve, he [enlightened her] He also gave hope to Adam, and the good news [of the] glorious [kingdom] He went up to the heights [of the aeons] of light.

Then the summons and the obedience, the great counsel that came to the elements, which are set in conjunction: it mixed with them, it was established in silence. It bears up [all things] until the end time when it can arise and stand firm in the great fire. It will gather to it its own soul, and sculpt it in the Last Statue. You will also find it sweeps out and casts from it the pollution that is foreign to it. However, the life and the light that are in all things it gathers in to it, and builds upon its body.

The time when this Last Statue will be perfect in all its limbs, then it can become free and ascend from that great struggle through the Living Spirit its father, the one who comes and brings a [...] limb. He brings it up from within this gathering (?), the melting down and destruction of all things.

Now, this counsel, that summons and obedience, resembles thus cooled butter. If a person will take and set it in hot milk, it melts down and soaks in with this hot milk. It melts in another time in silence and quiet to the midst [of the milk] yet also, of the power and the taste of this milk [...] is drawn to (the butter), and (the milk) sets and becomes cold [...] in [...] and the [...] this milk it shall clarify and discard. However, the oil and the grease and the 'beauty' of the milk it shall gather in to it.

Again, this too is what the advent of that thought is like, the counsel of life, which is the summons and obedience that came to the elements. This is the one that at the end can arise and stand firm, and will gather in to it all the lives, and the light that has remained behind in everything. It can build them upon its body; it will gather them in to it [and sculpts them] in its image for ever and ever [...] from this time.

fills.explanation: The phrase "revealed from him" matches the identical construction used in ¶4 ("revealed from the first greatness") and ¶6 ("revealed from him"), describing emanations proceeding from a higher divine degree.

The verb pair "spread out and established" is the chapter's standard formula for divine powers being distributed and fixed in their stations (cf. ¶3 "established in total twelve"), and the spiritual reading confirms "arranged in fives."

The editor's "sons" is correct in the natural-plane register: "five sons of the First Man" is the consistent Kephalaia designation throughout this chapter (¶4, ¶8, ¶16), corresponding to five faculties of the celestial human in the spiritual sense.

The five sons of the First Man constitute/support the cosmic edifice; the spiritual reading says they "constitute the whole spiritual edifice," and "support" is the natural-plane equivalent in the Kephalaia's architectural vocabulary of divine building.

The five sons of the Living Spirit are spread out to five cosmic stations "supporting all things" — the spiritual reading confirms "sustaining all things therein," and this matches the Kephalaia's cosmological doctrine of the five cosmic supports.

Jesus the Splendour appointed the summons and obedience as successors "over" the great earth — the spiritual reading says "within the great celestial good," and "over" expresses their appointed authority in the natural register.

The pairing "the great earth and the light" is fundamental Manichaean cosmology — the light-earth and the light imprisoned within it; the spiritual reading confirms something "abiding in them," and light is what abides within the created order.

The chapter follows a strict pattern where each divine figure's coming is introduced with "The advent also of..." (cf. ¶12 "the advent of the Living Spirit," ¶19 "The advent also of the Third Ambassador," ¶23 "The advent also of Jesus the Splendour").

The chapter introduces each advent with a standard parabolic formula (cf. ¶13 "is like this," ¶19 "is like a great king," ¶23 "just like a man"); ¶10 must likewise introduce the First Man's parable, and ¶11's summary "Just as with this man" confirms the comparison to "a man" was established here.

The parable describes a noble son (¶11) belonging to his father, which corresponds to the First Man belonging to the Father of Greatness — the fundamental filial relationship that establishes the son's original status in the kingdom.

The noble son existed "in a kingdom of great esteem" — the spiritual reading says "held in honor," and "of great" naturally connects "kingdom" to "esteem" to describe the son's original elevated status before his enemies assailed him.

The summary in ¶11 explicitly says "this noble son whose enemies surround him" — so the parable in ¶10 must have stated that "his enemies surrounded him," establishing the situation that ¶11 then recapitulates.

The enemies strip from the noble son "his glory and a richness" — "glory" pairs naturally with "richness" in the Kephalaia's vocabulary of spiritual plunder, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "spiritual abundance."

The editor's "him in" is grammatically correct and contextually necessary: "they imprison him in captivity" follows the standard construction of the chapter's description of enemies overpowering the noble son.

The spiritual reading says "prevailed by his humility," and the Kephalaia's theme of the First Man overcoming through patient endurance requires a verb of quiet triumph — "prevailed" fits the passage's emphasis on victory through humility and restraint.
The advent of the First Man happened "among the rulers, the enemies of the light" — "among the" introduces the hostile environment, matching the spiritual reading's "among the ruling evils."

The preceding sentence states the Living Spirit's advent "differs from that of the First Man," and this sentence restates the contrast: "His advent is not like the advent of the First Man" — a natural Kephalaia parallelism using synonymous phrasing.

The spiritual reading says "was severe and unyielding," requiring a copula to link the judge to his character description; "he is hard and cruel" provides the emphatic subject-copula construction natural to the Kephalaia's expository style.

The judge both punishes the guilty and aids the victim: "he gives the means to that man" (the noble son) completes the judicial function, echoing the chapter's repeated references to "that man, the noble son" (¶13, ¶15).

The escalation of judicial punishment moves from striking with whips to cutting off limbs to cutting off "heads" — the natural climax of bodily punishment in the parable's legal register, matching the spiritual reading's escalation of severing faculties.
The parable's judge "hangs by their feet" — this matches the cosmological application in ¶16 where "others he hung head down," which requires suspension by the feet.

The judge "kills them to flay their skin from them" — stripping the skin "from them" is the natural completion of the flaying image, corresponding to the spiritual reading's stripping away of external appearances.
The editor's "they for" correctly renders the demonstrative-relative construction: "they for whom it is fitting to banish" introduces the final category of punished evildoers in the judicial parable.

The passage lists categories of bound rulers using the repeated pattern "some of them... others..." (cf. ¶16: "some of them he enclosed," "others he hung"); "some of them are crucified" continues this established pattern.

The Living Spirit "established the judgements upon them" — i.e. upon the rulers/powers of Darkness — and then "He was revealed to all the powers of Darkness," making "upon them" the natural object of the judicial establishment.

The editor's "in respect of the" correctly links the judgment given to the rulers with the First Man as the aggrieved party: the Living Spirit judged the rulers "in respect of the First Man" — i.e. regarding the wrongs done to him.

The chain of judgment "became fixed in the earth till the end time" — the spiritual reading confirms "fixed in the natural order," and "fixed" is the Kephalaia's term for permanent binding of evil powers within the cosmic structure.
The parallel passage in ¶20 explicitly lists "the craftsmen and architects and artisans" — the king inspects these three categories, and GAP-40 fills the second item in this established triad.

The parallel passage in ¶20 explicitly lists "the craftsmen and architects and artisans" — GAP-41 fills the third item, completing the triad that describes the cosmic workers the great king (Third Ambassador) inspects.
The king "shall rejoice with great joy over them" — the joy is directed at the good workers, paralleling the Third Ambassador's delight upon inspecting the completed cosmic works described in ¶21.

The editor's "and completed" naturally pairs with "constructed": the artisans "constructed his works and completed his orders," forming a standard Kephalaia hendiadys for faithful execution of divine commands.

The editor's "his works" is confirmed by the direct parallel in the preceding parable: "this great king who comes and inspects his works and fortifications" — when the Third Ambassador comes, he likewise "saw his works established and prepared."

The Third Ambassador saw two things: (1) his works established and prepared, and (2) also the series of rulers — "also the" introduces the second object of "he saw," connecting the parallel lists of what was prepared above and below.

The Third Ambassador praises the Living Spirit: "The judgement that you have given is good" — "given" echoes "you gave to them correspondingly" in the next clause, and "is" provides the copula linking judgment to its evaluation as "good."

The speech continues praising the Living Spirit's judicial acts: "what you uttered is just; you gave to them correspondingly" — "just" fits the chapter's pervasive theme of righteous judgment and completes the evaluation begun by "good" in the preceding clause.

Jesus the Splendour "came to all things" — this universal scope matches both the garden parable (dealing with an entire fig-garden) and the cosmological application in ¶25 where he works "in the zone, among the many powers, until he reached the form of the flesh."

The gardening parable requires an object for "pull out" before transitioning to "burn": "pull out a bad tree and burn a difficult fig-garden" — "bad tree" echoes "the bad trees" mentioned immediately after, and "and" provides the conjunction to "burn."

After cutting the bad trees with an axe, the gardener "pulled out their roots and their body with his fire" — uprooting roots is the natural correlate of cutting trees, ensuring false growths cannot regenerate, matching the spiritual reading's "their very substance."

The clause concludes with finality: the bad trees shall not "bear fruit bad to eat any more" — completing the temporal finality established by "from this time" in the preceding clause about sprouting, and matching the spiritual reading's sense of permanent cessation.

The partial word gap + "-ness" forms "righteousness": Jesus the Splendour acts "in his righteousness as a king and a saviour," consistent with the chapter's pervading theme of righteous judgment and the spiritual reading's emphasis on sovereign redemptive justice.

The editor's "He perfected" correctly describes Jesus the Splendour's completion of his saving work in Eve: "He perfected his will in Eve" — the divine illuminating wisdom brought its purpose to fulfillment in the receptive faculty of the first humanity.

Jesus the Splendour's salvific work follows the Manichaean pattern of awakening and illuminating the first humans; "enlightened her" parallels "gave hope to Adam" in the next clause, with Eve receiving knowledge and Adam receiving hope — the two complementary salvific acts.

The phrase "the good news of the glorious [kingdom]" requires the preposition "of the" to connect "good news" to the subsequent adjective-noun phrase, forming a standard proclamation formula in the Kephalaia.

"The good news of the glorious kingdom" is the standard Manichaean eschatological proclamation — the glad tidings given to Adam concern the Kingdom of Light to which the soul will return, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "glorious purpose."

"He went up to the heights of the aeons of light" is standard Manichaean cosmological vocabulary — the aeons of light are the elevated divine realms to which Jesus the Splendour ascends, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "elevated states of wisdom."

The counsel "bears up all things until the end time" — the summons and obedience, mixed silently with the elements, sustains and preserves all that has life and light until the final consummation, paralleling the butter that silently pervades and sustains the milk.

The butter "melts in silence and quiet to the midst of the milk" — the butter analogy requires specifying that it penetrates to the center of the milk, which is the substance being worked upon, directly stated in the surrounding context.

The counsel "gathers them in and sculpts them in its image" — this directly echoes ¶26's "sculpt it in the Last Statue," using the chapter's own vocabulary for the final forming of all gathered light-lives into the completed divine human image.
